item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 treats the old 1br0/1ez3 entries as partial syntaxin N-terminal-domain instances, not as standalone evidence that syntaxin is a spectrin-repeat protein. 1br0 chain A is SID d1br0a_, and 1ez3 chains A/B/C are d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, and d1ez3c_; all four are classified as all-alpha proteins, STAT-like fold a.47, t-SNARE-proteins superfamily a.47.2, t-SNARE-proteins family a.47.2.1, with the protein node \"Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain\" for the manually curated rat entries. Each of those fragment SIDs carries the SCOPe comment \"three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat\" and the domain-level ms caveat: it is missing secondary-structure elements that make up less than one third of the common domain. 1dn1 chain B, SID d1dn1b_, is also in a.47.2.1 and has no ms fragment caveat in the current record; in 2.08 it is an automated match to the full rat syntaxin representative d3c98b_. The biological reading is therefore: the 1br0 and 1ez3 fragments can support membership in the syntaxin/t-SNARE family when interpreted with the missing-structure caveat, but their three-helix resemblance to one spectrin repeat should not be promoted into spectrin-repeat family homology, spectrin function transfer, exact whole-domain boundaries, or a preferred modeling template for the complete N-terminal domain.
